previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with chronic pancreatitis and a history of polysubstance abuse and depression, was admitted with severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and hypotension. She was found to be in septic shock due to a C. difficile infection, with acute on chronic pancreatitis contributing to her condition. She was initially managed in the ICU with IV fluids, antibiotics (Flagyl and vancomycin), and pain control per her established protocol. A left internal jugular catheter was replaced with a right PICC line for reliable access. Her course improved with resolution of sepsis, normalization of labs, and tolerance of oral intake and medications. She was discharged home on a full 14-day course of oral antibiotics and her baseline medications, with instructions to complete treatment and follow up with primary care.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
